rationale: Both largely miss the ground truth's actual (shallow, stylistic) reviewer comments, instead independently converging on a substantive num_stale_output_tokens double-seeding bug, which cross-validates that finding as real. Y edges out on precision via its 'Confirmed'-tagged, source-quoted evidence and a disciplined sweep that explicitly rules out false leads (test_compile.py, qwen2_5_omni_thinker.py), plus a more thorough arg_utils.py enumeration citing ~10 affected classes by file:line; Y also touches the parallel_state.py/use_all2all topic the human reviewer flagged, giving it a slim recall edge. X is somewhat more actionable with fuller proposed code diffs, but includes harder-to-verify claims (CI gate colors, a claimed 105-test run, simulated repro output) that weigh against precision.
